body.x: Seon Electronics (CEO Lee Chang-seop, www.seon-kr.com) introduced its ‘Karmi2’, an IoT-based automatic pet feeder, in the joint pavilion of the Mobile Technology Convergence Center (MTCC) at the world’s best IT technology exhibition ‘CES(Consumer Technology Show) 2016’ which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas Convention Center(LVCC).

The product integrates a camera and a pet feeder. By using a smartphone, it enables users to give pet food automatically when they want and how much they want. It is extremely convenient as users can feed their pets when they are away from their homes. And they can check on their pets via an attached camera, which works with a smartphone application through Wi-Fi.

Combining a camera and a pet food dispenser, it is equipped with an IR remote control function. It is suitable for small and medium-sized pets. Users can download the Karmi app on Google Play and Apple’s App Store.

The company also showcased the Seon Gas Valve Controller. The product is controlled with an app, and it checks for gas leaks and provides a shutoff timer function for valves. If the gas sensor detects a leak, it immediately shuts down the valve and warns the users via a message.

Seon Electronics CEO Lee Chang-seop said: “We are happy to introduce our outstanding domestic IoT technology and products at CES 2016. We consider this exhibition as an opportunity to further enter foreign markets, including the U.S.”

The company possesses various technologies for the design and production of products that utilize wireless network technology, such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and various MCU and sensors, including STM32. It is focusing on the IoT business based on up-to-date technologies.

MTCC prepared the joint pavilion at this exhibition and supported related domestic companies’ participation in CES 2016, promoting the smart venture school of Kyungpook National University. It is mainly focused on the competitiveness reinforcement business of new mobile convergence in the global market.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), CES 2016 is the world's largest exhibition to see the latest global trends in electronics and IT industry in one spot.

AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES for 11 years to introduce the new technologies and products. After the local coverage and research, AVING News will hold ‘CES 2016 Review Conference’ in AVING Studio, Korea on January 28th.
